source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Trading Range

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: TradingRangeEquidistantScalpTarget
candidates.quote: Try to keep your potential reward at least as large as your risk so your winning percentage does not have to be 70 percent or higher... they should trade only if they are holding for at least a two-point profit.
candidates.description: In a trading range, size the profit target to be at least as large as the initial risk (an 'equidistant move'), so the trade's win rate need not be high to be profitable.
candidates.pseudocode:
// same shape as the catalog's TakeProfitWithRatioStop with ratio = 1
ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= riskDollars || ctx.OpenPositionProfit() <= -riskDollars
candidates.book_order_type: profit-limit order placed a distance from entry equal to (or greater than) the distance risked to the stop

complexity.reason: identical shape to the existing TakeProfitWithRatioStop rule; the only new content is Brooks's trading-range rationale for a 1:1 ratio

notes: Kept for recall even though numerically identical to TakeProfitWithRatioStop(ratio=1); Brooks frames it specifically as the trading-range scalping rule.

candidates.name: ExtendedRangeMoveFavorsFadeFilter
candidates.quote: If the market has been going up for five to 10 bars in a trading range, it is usually far better to look only for shorts and to take profits on longs. If it has been going down for a while, look to buy or to take profits on shorts.
candidates.description: Inside a trading range, once price has made an extended net move in one direction over the last several bars without reversing, treat further with-move entries as low-quality and favor entries (or profit-taking) in the opposite direction instead.

complexity.reason: cross-bar net-move measurement composed with the research-grade trading-range regime detector

notes: Brooks gives a range (5 to 10 bars); default picks the midpoint, treat as an optimizable input.
The net-move test itself is structurally identical to the catalog's Momentum rule, gated by the trading-range regime.

candidates.name: BuyHigh2NearRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying a high 2 near the bottom of the range. These are often second attempts to reverse the market up from the bottom, like a double bottom. Selling a low 2 near the top of the range.
candidates.description: Take a High 2 long setup (a second bull-reversal attempt near a prior low, resembling a double bottom) only when it forms near the bottom of the current trading range.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the High 2 signal bar

complexity.reason: composes the High2Setup pattern (already moderate/hard elsewhere) with a simple range-extreme location test

notes: Brooks states H2-near-bottom and L2-near-top as an explicit mirror pair in one breath; one mirrored candidate covers both.
Depends on High2Setup, defined across trends chapters 10/15/21 (T10-23, T15-19, T21-72) and R11-26 (TradingRangeEntryNearRangeExtremeOnly, chapter 11 of this book) for the location filter.

candidates.name: BuyRangeExtremeSecondEntryAfterTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: Buying at the bottom of a trading range, especially if it is a second entry after a break above a bear trend line. Shorting at the top of a trading range, especially if it is a second entry after a break below the bull trend line.
candidates.description: Entry near the range low that is also a second attempt following a break of a minor bear trend line (or, mirrored, near the range high following a break of a minor bull trend line).
candidates.pseudocode:
nearBottom = close[0] <= rangeLow + nearExtremeAtr * atr(atrLookback);
enterLongNextBarOpen = nearBottom && isSecondEntry[0] && brokeAboveMinorBearTrendLine[0];
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the second-entry signal bar

complexity.reason: needs a minor trend-line break (pivot + line projection), a second-entry counter, and the range-extreme location test

notes: Trend-line break primitive is likely defined in trends chapter 13 (Trend Lines); second-entry counting in trends chapter 10 (Second Entries).

candidates.name: BuyWedgeBullFlagNearRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying a wedge bull flag near the bottom. Selling a wedge bear flag near the top.
candidates.description: Take a wedge (three-push) bull-flag entry only when it forms near the bottom of the current trading range.
candidates.pseudocode:
nearBottom = close[0] <= rangeLow + nearExtremeAtr * atr(atrLookback);
enterLongNextBarOpen = isThreePushWedgeBullFlag[0] && nearBottom;
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the third push's signal bar

complexity.reason: inherits the three-push wedge pattern's swing-pivot detection (R18-01) plus the range-location test

candidates.name: BuyReversalBarAfterSwingBreakAtRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying a bull reversal bar or reversal pattern like a final flag (discussed in book 3) after a break below a swing low at the bottom of the range.
candidates.description: After price breaks below a recent swing low near the bottom of the trading range, buy a subsequent bull reversal bar or final-flag reversal pattern.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar / final-flag signal bar

complexity.reason: needs swing-low detection, a reversal-bar or final-flag pattern test, and the range-location filter

notes: Reversal-bar primitive defined in trends chapter 5 (Signal Bars, Reversal Bars); final-flag primitives R03-10 and R05-19 in this book.

candidates.name: BuyBreakoutPullbackNearRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying a breakout pullback after an upside breakout near the bottom of the range (for example, if the market starts up and pulls back, look to buy above the high of the prior bar).
candidates.description: After an upside breakout that occurs near the bottom of the trading range, buy the pullback one tick above the high of the prior (pullback) bar.
candidates.pseudocode:
nearBottom = close[0] <= rangeLow + nearExtremeAtr * atr(atrLookback);
enterLongNextBarOpen = isBreakoutPullbackBuyEntry[0] && nearBottom;
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the pullback bar

complexity.reason: composes the existing breakout-pullback entry (R05-04 / RP1-04) with the range-location test

candidates.name: BuySpikeAtRangeBottomLimitEntry
candidates.quote: Buying a bear spike at the market or on a limit order at or below the low of the prior swing low at the bottom of the range (entering in spikes requires a wider stop and the spike happens quickly, so this combination is difficult for many traders).
candidates.description: During a bear spike that is testing or breaking the bottom of the trading range, buy at the market or on a limit order at/below the low of the prior swing low.
candidates.book_order_type: market order or resting limit order at/below the prior swing low

complexity.reason: needs a spike-classification primitive plus swing-low tracking and the wider-stop sizing Brooks calls for

notes: Brooks flags this as an advanced, difficult-to-execute combination (requires a wider stop and fast fills); recorded as stated, not endorsed.

candidates.name: BuyClimaxExhaustionTrendBarAtRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying at the close or below the low of a large bear trend bar near the bottom of the range, since it is often an exhaustive sell climax and the end of the sell-off in a trading range.
candidates.description: Treat an unusually large bear trend bar near the bottom of the trading range as a likely exhaustive sell climax, and buy at its close or on a limit order below its low.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the close of, or below the low of, the large bear trend bar

complexity.reason: a bar-size (body vs ATR) test combined with the range-location test

notes: Mirror-image test of BodyBelowAtrFraction (large instead of small body relative to ATR).

candidates.name: BuyWeakSignalBarLimitAtRangeBottom
candidates.quote: Buying at or below a low 1 or 2 weak signal bar on a limit order at the bottom of a trading range. Shorting at or above a high 1 or 2 weak signal bar on a limit order at the top of a trading range.
candidates.description: When a Low 1 or Low 2 short-setup signal bar is weak (poor follow-through quality) and forms at the bottom of the trading range, fade it by buying at or below its low on a limit order rather than expecting the short to work.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at or below the low of the weak signal bar

complexity.reason: needs a Low1/Low2 setup classifier and a signal-bar-quality score, composed with the range-location test

notes: 'Weak' signal-bar quality has no single stated formula in this chapter; a design decision is needed for the quality score itself (e.g., small body, long tail against the direction, poor close position).

candidates.name: BuyCounterCloseAtStrongSwingStart
candidates.quote: Buying a bear close at the start of a strong bull swing. Selling a bull close at the start of a strong bear swing.
candidates.description: Right at the start of a swing judged strong enough to keep going, buy at the close of a bar that itself closed down (a small dip within the new swing), rather than waiting for a bull signal bar.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the close of the counter-direction bar

complexity.reason: "the start of a strong bull swing" is not given a bar-level test in this chapter; a design decision akin to always-in-direction is needed first

candidates.name: AvoidStopEntriesInMiddleOfRangeFilter
candidates.quote: Rarely enter on stops in the middle of the range, but it is sometimes reasonable to enter on limit orders there. ... since the overall day was in a larger trading range and the market was now in the middle of that larger range, traders were hesitant to buy.
candidates.description: While the market is in a trading range, block stop (breakout-style) entries whose signal bar closes near the middle third of the range; entries there, if taken, should be limit orders only.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (blocks stop entries; limit entries in the middle are still permitted)

complexity.reason: a range-midpoint distance test on top of the trading-range regime detector

notes: middleZoneHalfWidth = 0.17 makes the excluded band roughly the middle third of the range; a reading of 'the middle', not a stated number.

candidates.name: SessionAverageBarRangeMoneyStop
candidates.quote: Some traders would have used a money stop, like around the height of an average bar so far today, maybe 10 to 15 cents.
candidates.description: Size the protective stop as a multiple of the average bar range observed so far in the current session, rather than a fixed dollar amount or a rolling multi-day ATR.
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop order at entry price minus the sized distance

complexity.reason: needs a session-relative running average of bar range that resets at each new session, distinct from the corpus's rolling multi-bar ATR

notes: Distinct from AtrTrailingStop/AtrBandBreakout because the averaging window is 'so far today' (session-relative and growing), not a fixed rolling N-bar window.

candidates.name: ReversalCountInFirstHourPredictsTradingRangeDay
candidates.quote: Whenever the market has four or five reversals in the first hour, the odds of a trading range day increase.
candidates.description: Count directional reversals (swing-direction changes) within the first hour of the session; a high count raises the probability that the day will be a trading-range day, favoring range-style (fade/scalp) entries over breakout entries for the rest of the session.

complexity.reason: "reversal" has no single stated bar-level test here; needs swing-pivot detection or a reversal-bar definition before this can be coded, plus a session-bar-count convention that depends on the chart's bar size

notes: firstHourBars=12 assumes 5-minute bars; the parameter must be resized for the chart's actual bar interval.

candidates.name: OpeningBarDojiPredictsTradingRangeDay
candidates.quote: The first bar of the day was a doji, and that increased the chances of a trading range day.
candidates.description: If the very first bar of the session is a doji, treat that as a (weak) signal favoring a trading-range day, persisted as a day-context flag.

complexity.reason: a single-bar doji test on the session's first bar, latched for the rest of the session

notes: Doji body-fraction primitive is likely already defined in trends chapter 2 (Trend Bars, Doji Bars, and Climaxes); reuse that definition on the first bar of the session.

rejected.quote: they should take trading range trades only where they believe the probability of success of an equidistant move is at least 60 percent
rejected.reason: requires a subjective probability-of-success estimate, not a value decidable from OHLCV bars

rejected.quote: Reversing is too difficult for most traders, and instead they should use profit targets for exits and then look for a trade in the opposite direction.
rejected.reason: describes trader workflow/psychology, not a bar-level test; the pane system already separates exits from new entries

rejected.quote: Only the long limit orders at one tick above the low got filled, which means that the bulls were very aggressive.
rejected.reason: requires knowledge of which resting limit orders in the market actually got filled -- order-book data the engine does not have

rejected.quote: Everyone is different, but there are often clues early on, and as more accumulate, traders become more confident.
rejected.reason: pure discretion, no bar-level test proposed

chapter_summary: Chapter 21 is a worked example of trading a QQQ trading-range day, opening with a checklist of range trade setups (all keyed to entering near the range extremes, mostly composites of already-defined patterns -- High 2/Low 2, wedge flags, breakout pullbacks, final flags, climax bars, weak signal bars -- gated by a near-range-extreme location filter) and closing with a bar-by-bar narrative. Distinctive new material: an equidistant (1:1 reward:risk) scalp-target rationale, a rule to fade extended same-direction moves inside a range, a filter against stop entries in the middle of the range, a session-relative average-bar-range money stop, and two early trading-range-day predictors (first-hour reversal count, opening-bar doji) that are graded research/simple respectively. Most of the narrative's bar-specific commentary illustrates primitives this book and the trends book already define (H2/L2, spike and channel, tight-range magnetic pull, dueling lines, triangles) and was not re-recorded.
